rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 2012, <cite id="5">the Center for Islamic Teachings and Community Development</cite> operates religious education and social programs in the Chicagoland area. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $1,955,187</cite> while executing its core mission. Its primary initiatives center on <cite id="5">Islamic education through Abraar Academy</cite>, funeral support via the American Muslim Cemetery, and local community service programs. The charity is <cite id="2">zakat-eligible</cite> and utilizes zakat donations to fund free education for needy students and distribute Ramadan meals [5]. Based on financial filings, the organization maintained a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 100.0%</cite> in FY2024, directing all recorded spending directly into program operations. However, data confidence remains low due to limited public transparency. Financial records also indicate significant capital retention, with <cite id="1">126.5 months of working capital</cite> held in reserves. While this provides long-term financial stability, holding substantial reserves presents a balancing consideration for a zakat-collecting institution.
